summary.intent: Run the GSD discuss-phase workflow for CipherBox Phase 69 ("FUSE and WinFsp — Rust Integration and Grant-Root Awareness") to scout the codebase, surface undecided gray areas, and lock implementation decisions into a 69-CONTEXT.md for downstream research/planning agents.
summary.outcome: Produced and committed 69-CONTEXT.md and 69-DISCUSSION-LOG.md capturing 8 locked decisions (68.2 reference sourcing, core/sdk placement, durable floor design, Node enum cutover, in-phase rotation engine port, isolated WinFsp plan, write-plane dual-keying constraint, and carried-forward Q3/grant-root items) plus reviewed/folded related todos.

repo: crates/core in cipher-box still uses the legacy FolderMetadata/FileMetadata/FilePointer/FolderEntry types — the node/v3 Node enum model has not landed in Rust yet, so Phase 69 is a full model port, not just a crypto swap.
There is no rotate_read/grant_root implementation anywhere in the Rust stack yet.
crates/crypto already has the needed primitives (seal_aes_gcm_aad, unseal_aes_gcm_aad, build_node_aad) from Phase 61.
crates/sdk (Rust) already exists with client/sync/state/queue — satisfies the 'dedicated Rust SDK crate' need.
The FUSE journal is an on-disk sidecar directory — planned as the natural location for the new durable anti-rollback floor store.

Phase 68.2 (TS read-chain consolidation that Phase 69 mirrors) is roadmap-listed but not executed — no phase dir, STATE still at 68.1; its planning docs exist only on branch origin/feat/sdk-owned-read-chain-and-resolved-folder-listings, which is checked out in the main worktree, so it must be read via `git show <ref>:<path>`, never `git checkout`.

68.2's CONTEXT.md defines the contract Phase 69 must mirror: ResolvedChild = {ipnsName, name, kind, size?, modifiedAt, sequence}; SDK model is imperative pull (listFolder/listSharedFolder) + folder:updated event push; DurableFloorStore maps to the existing RotationHighWater + HighWaterStore seam gated via RotationHighWater.enforceResolved.

Phase 65 Q3 already decided the authority model: write-recipient delete/move unlinks+bins with no cross-principal revoke, owner reconcile+rotation re-derives dangling grants (Model (a)) — Phase 69 mirrors this on the FUSE side rather than re-deciding it.
workflow: The GSD discuss-phase workflow scouts the codebase (crate layout, call sites, prior phase decisions) before presenting gray areas, explicitly to avoid re-asking questions already decided in earlier phases (e.g., Phase 65 Q3).

A todo-matcher tool returned 69 keyword-broad hits when checking for related todos; most were off-topic and had to be manually filtered down to ~4 genuinely relevant items before presenting to the user.
Commits in this repo/workflow are guarded with a timeout due to a known 1Password SSH-signing hang.

friction: Todo-matching tool is noisy — returns broad keyword matches (69 hits) requiring manual filtering to find genuinely relevant items.
68.2's planning docs are only accessible on a feature branch that's checked out in the main worktree, forcing use of `git show` instead of a normal checkout to avoid disrupting the working tree.
Known recurring 1Password SSH-signing hang requires wrapping commit commands with a timeout.
open_items: Grant-root scope-computation algorithm explicitly deferred to a plan-time design pass rather than decided during this discuss-phase session.
Phase 68.2 itself is still unexecuted (no phase dir, plans TBD) even though Phase 69 will build against its (branch-only) contract now.
WinFsp support scoped as its own separate plan to be executed manually on a Windows machine, gated by the 'Cargo Check & Test (Windows)' CI job as sign-off authority.
Write-plane dual-keying flagged as a hard constraint requiring a security-review pass.
Todo item 'replay-reuse-verified-parent-sequence' was folded/deferred rather than included in this phase's scope.
